findings.claim: Unrelated change: MessagePackSecurity.UntrustedData MaximumObjectGraphDepth is raised from 500 to 5000, a tenfold weakening of the stack-depth DoS protection. It has nothing to do with the generator/analyzer crash in REQ-2283. The ledger records a deliberate depth limit of 500 even for trusted data.

receipt_plan.detail: [L9] records secure-by-default history and a stack depth limit of 500 even for untrusted/trusted data. Cite this against the 500->5000 change. Also run a test that deserializes 501-deep nested data with UntrustedData and expects MessagePackSerializationException.

findings.claim: The new ReportIfLocatedInCompilation filter drops every diagnostic whose location is not in a syntax tree of the compilation, so it also silences diagnostics with no location (Location.None). For a metadata type, MemberNeedsKey now gets a null location and is silently dropped. This is consistent with the documented behavior that diagnostics for referenced-assembly types are not reported by the consumer.

receipt_plan.detail: [L8] Types from referenced assemblies are deliberately not analysed by the compiling assembly. A missing diagnostic for such a type is not a defect.

findings.claim: The README and MsgPack004.md additions document new behavior. The README section is placed under the custom-formatter mixing section, not the generic-type or analyzer docs, and says closed generic value types from other assemblies work. This matches the requirement, but the placement is questionable.

receipt_plan.detail: Check that the README subsection 'Generic types from referenced assemblies' sits logically under the Analyzer/formatter section. It was inserted just before MagicOnion.
